reference: Bash's built-in type/help metadata behavior plus the documented wgetch API and timing contract in the published wgetch interface and the existing API smoke contract in the terminal API contract. There is no matching GNU CLI for this loadable, so no operation parity is claimed.
coverage: Private regular-file descriptor decoding of bytes, control aliases, complete ANSI sequences and EOF.
Parent-shell screen lifecycle, pushback ordering, repeated peek, empty/full queues and missing operands.
Timed ESC delivery remains deferred to a deterministic PTY or clock/poll mock.
exclusions: No matching GNU CLI; records use fixed documented key codes and ncurses-style pushback contracts.
Delayed-byte timing, all 16 simultaneous screen slots and every ANSI sequence are not established by the bounded cases. Timed ESC behavior requires the deferred PTY/mock fixture.

cases.purpose: Check Bash's documented type -t result for a loadable builtin without invoking wgetch operations.
Check the Bash help metadata against wgetch's documented command forms and advertised ESC timing contract.
cases.script: h=$(help wgetch); [[ $h == *'wgetch open [FD] [NAME]'* && $h == *'wgetch read HANDLE|FD'* && $h == *'wgetch unget HANDLE CODE'* && $h == *'wgetch peek HANDLE'* && $h == *'wgetch close HANDLE'* && $h == *'wgetch list'* && $h == *'50 ms ESC grace'* && $h == *'ESCDELAY'* && $h == *'max(400 ms'* ]] && printf 'documented help surface\n'

cases.purpose: Decode printable, DEL/BS, CR/LF, TAB and EOF from a private regular-file descriptor. Expected records use the documented key-code contract; no terminal is needed.
cases.script:
printf 'A\177\010\015\012\011' > keys
exec 3< keys
for item in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do wgetch read 3; done
exec 3<&-
cases.stdout:
char 65
backspace 263
backspace 263
enter 264
enter 264
tab 269
none 0

cases.purpose: Decode complete ANSI CSI/SS3 arrow, function, shifted arrow and paste delimiter sequences from a private descriptor against fixed key-code mappings. Timed delivery is separate.
cases.script:
printf '\033[A\033OP\033[1;2D\033[200~\033[201~' > keys
exec 3< keys
for item in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do wgetch read 3; done
exec 3<&-
cases.stdout:
key_up 257
key_f1 272
key_s_left 306
paste_start 288
paste_end 289
none 0

cases.purpose: Deferred check of lone ESC grace, delayed continuation, ambiguous exact-prefix sequences, and the max(400 ms, ESCDELAY*8) total cap.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r4: Not reachable through the candidate interface: the fixed wgetch.c bw_keys table (no fixture or terminfo loading) contains no exact key that is also a prefix of a longer key (e.g. ESC[20~ and ESC[200~ diverge at byte 5), so the exact-vs-longer resolution path in bw_read_key_fd cannot be triggered by any input. Requires a candidate key-table extension, not a fixture.; r5: Not observable: the longest wgetch key is 6 bytes and the cap timer starts after the second byte, so at most 4 further bytes each within one 50 ms slice arrive in under 200 ms, below the 400 ms minimum cap; any slower trickle ends on the 50 ms slice first. The cap can never be the deciding condition with the fixed table (kgetch's fixture-extensible table is covered by migration-kgetch-total-cap-*).

cases.purpose: Check persistent open/list/close state, pushback stack order, nondestructive peek, empty-queue status and EOF on a private descriptor. Keep open in the parent shell so the handle survives.
cases.script:
: > keys
exec 3< keys
wgetch open 3 fixture > handle
h=$(<handle)
[[ $h == 1 ]]
wgetch list
wgetch unget "$h" 65
wgetch unget "$h" 66
wgetch peek "$h"
wgetch peek "$h"
wgetch read "$h"
wgetch read "$h"
if wgetch peek "$h"; then exit 90; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]
wgetch read "$h"
wgetch close "$h"
wgetch list
exec 3<&-
cases.stdout:
1 3 fixture depth=0
char 66
char 66
char 66
char 65
none 0

cases.purpose: Missing required operands are usage errors, and closing an unknown handle fails. These pure argument/state checks do not read any input descriptor.
cases.script:
for verb in 'close' 'unget' 'peek' 'read'; do
 if wgetch "$verb"; then exit 90; else rc=$?; fi
 printf '%s:%s\n' "$verb" "$rc"
 [[ $rc -eq 2 ]]
done
if wgetch close 999; then exit 91; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'unknown-close:%s\n' "$rc"
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]

cases.purpose: The documented 64-entry pushback boundary rejects one extra item without disturbing the retained queue.
cases.script:
: > keys
exec 3< keys
wgetch open 3 fixture > handle
h=$(<handle)
for ((i=0;i<64;i++)); do wgetch unget "$h" 65; done
if wgetch unget "$h" 66; then exit 90; else rc=$?; fi
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]
wgetch list
wgetch read "$h"
wgetch close "$h"
exec 3<&-
